preamble: Retroflexion of the dental/alveolar voiced stop [d] to [ɖ]. In Indo-Aryan it occurs by assimilation to a preceding retroflex (Sanskrit nīḍa 'nest' < *niẓḍás) and sporadically word-initially in Middle Indo-Aryan (Sanskrit dáśati 'bites' > Prakrit ḍasaï > Hindi ḍasnā). In Swedish and Norwegian, /r/ followed by /d/ coalesces into [ɖ] by the sandhi process called retroflexion.

examples.to: Prakrit ḍasaï > Hindi डसना ḍasnā /ɖəsnɑː/ 'to bite (of a snake), sting'
examples.note: Unconditioned initial retroflexion of dental d in Middle Indo-Aryan.
The d became retroflex by assimilation to the preceding RUKI-retroflexed sibilant *ẓ, which was then lost with compensatory lengthening; cognate with Latin nīdus, English nest.
/r/ + /d/ coalesce into retroflex [ɖ]; the process also applies across word boundaries.
